definition: A candidate inference-time effect in which repeated, visible and structured epistemic relations in a task environment may help a model infer local rules about what supports what, which transitions are not licensed, and when uncertainty must be retained, with possible effects on later answers.

alternative_explanations.label: in-context learning
alternative_explanations.description: The model may infer a task or response mapping from examples without any special governance structure.
alternative_explanations.disambiguation_test: Match examples, token budget and task format while varying whether the state-transition relations are present.

alternative_explanations.label: task inference
alternative_explanations.description: The model may infer that the evaluator rewards cautious answers from the general task framing.
alternative_explanations.disambiguation_test: Use neutral instructions and held-out domains, then separate exposure from challenge wording and scoring.

alternative_explanations.label: structural priming
alternative_explanations.description: Repeated relation patterns may prime a form of continuation without inducing a governance-specific boundary.
alternative_explanations.disambiguation_test: Compare delexicalized relation exposure with content-matched prose and test delayed transfer.

alternative_explanations.label: style imitation
alternative_explanations.description: The model may copy hedges, headings or cautious wording while leaving the decision boundary unchanged.
alternative_explanations.disambiguation_test: Score unauthorized transitions and licensed conclusions separately from surface style similarity.

alternative_explanations.label: terminology imitation
alternative_explanations.description: The model may repeat terms such as unknown or evidence ceiling without respecting their relationships.
alternative_explanations.disambiguation_test: Treat terminology leakage as an independent metric and include terminology-only controls.

alternative_explanations.label: default alignment or caution
alternative_explanations.description: A model may already prefer calibrated and cautious answers independently of the exposure material.
alternative_explanations.disambiguation_test: Use a no-exposure baseline across the same synthetic packets and report deltas rather than absolute caution.

alternative_explanations.label: contextual mimicry
alternative_explanations.description: The model may infer a local persona or discourse norm rather than a transferable evidence boundary.
alternative_explanations.disambiguation_test: Use unrelated delayed-transfer cases and challenge pressure that rewards direct overclaiming.

claim_ceiling: The record defines a research candidate and repository protocol, not a confirmed causal mechanism.
Any observed change is bounded to the tested model, context, prompt, benchmark, language and run configuration.
No result establishes permanent learning, weight change, a new law, external validity or first discovery.
Repository tests demonstrate tool and contract behavior; they do not establish an ESI effect in a live model.
Soft exposure can never grant permission, truth, M/E, Owner authority, epistemic acceptance or safety release.
falsification_criteria: Delexicalized structure does not outperform terminology-only, style-matched or broken-structure controls on boundary adherence.
The apparent effect occurs only in one model, one context length, one language or one prompt family.
Adversarial direct-overclaim pressure removes the effect across the tested exposure arms.
Blinded annotation agreement cannot distinguish decision-boundary behavior from style or terminology imitation.
Improved caution is paired with unacceptable loss of licensed conclusions, usefulness or task completion.
Independent replication or relevant primary literature provides a better explanation that does not require ESI.
